summary.allegation: The issuer says the cardholder did not authorise the 87.40 GBP payment to QuickStream Digital on 29 April 2025, that the card was in the cardholder's possession at the time, and that the cardholder has no relationship with the merchant.
summary.to_defend: Mastercard requires any two of: full AVS plus CVV match, successful 3D Secure authentication, two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder, or signed proof of delivery to the billing address.

requirements.title: AVS and CVV match
requirements.text: AVS match (full address) AND CVV match on the disputed transaction.
requirements.finding: Authorisation data for txn_7762GH shows avs_result N (no address match) and cvv_result N (no CVV match), so neither half of this requirement is met.
requirements.gap: No AVS or CVV match exists on the disputed authorisation.

requirements.title: 3DS authenticated
requirements.text: 3D Secure authentication completed successfully (Mastercard SecureCode / Identity Check).
requirements.finding: The transaction metadata records three_ds_status as not_attempted, so no Mastercard Identity Check authentication was performed.
requirements.gap: No 3D Secure authentication was carried out at the time of the transaction and none can be created after the fact.

requirements.title: Two prior undisputed transactions
requirements.text: Two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder with this merchant in the past 12 months, with matching billing details.
requirements.finding: No prior transaction history was supplied, and the merchant's own screening report states the customer account age is New (first transaction), which rules out two prior undisputed transactions.
requirements.gap: There are no earlier transactions from this cardholder with this merchant to evidence.

requirements.title: Signed delivery to billing address
requirements.text: Proof of delivery to the cardholder's billing address with signature.
requirements.finding: MCC 5815 is digital media and the transaction carries no shipping address (shipping_address_postcode: None), so nothing was physically shipped and signed proof of delivery cannot exist.

documents.label: Merchant internal fraud screening report
documents.reason: An internal risk score and conclusion of legitimacy is the merchant's own opinion, not AVS/CVV, 3DS, prior transaction or delivery evidence; it addresses none of R1 to R4.

alerts.text: The issuer states the cardholder has no relationship with the merchant and the merchant's own report confirms a new account on its first transaction, so there is no history to rebut the claim; confirm no other customer record exists under this billing postcode E14 5AB.

D1 is dated 12 May 2025, the day after the 11 May 2025 chargeback, so it was produced for the dispute rather than at the time of the transaction; check whether any contemporaneous screening record exists for 29 April 2025.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence
notes: Conflicting evidence flagged; it does not make accepting riskier

checks.label: No requirement is partly met, so accepting isn't borderline
Key evidence comes from document text, not only from an image
Images the evidence relies on are fully legible
Every quoted passage was found in the documents
The rule check and the AI recommendation agree

justification: Accept liability: R1 fails on avs_result N and cvv_result N, R2 fails on three_ds_status not_attempted, R3 fails as this was the account's first transaction and R4 cannot apply, so the two-requirement threshold cannot be reached.
rationale:
The issuer alleges the 87.40 GBP transaction txn_7762GH of 29 April 2025 was not authorised and that the cardholder has no relationship with QuickStream Digital.
Authorisation data shows no address match (AVS N), no CVV match (CVV N) and no 3D Secure attempt, so R1 and R2 both fail on facts that cannot be changed.
The merchant's own screening report records the customer account age as New (first transaction), so the two prior undisputed transactions required by R3 do not exist.
R4 cannot apply because MCC 5815 is digital media with no shipping address recorded, so no signed delivery proof is possible.
With zero of the required two conditions met and a new device fingerprint and 03:42 UTC timing supporting the fraud claim, the case is not defensible and liability should be accepted.
